response.sql: WITH j AS (SELECT u.acctscope AS acctscope, f.feerate - f.rebrate AS net_rate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault JOIN users u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp), s AS (SELECT acctscope, AVG(net_rate) AS avg_net_rate, COUNT(*) AS fee_record_count FROM j GROUP BY acctscope) SELECT acctscope, avg_net_rate, fee_record_count, avg_net_rate - AVG(avg_net_rate) OVER () AS diff_from_avg_of_scope_avgs FROM s

assumptions.assumption: The fee record count includes every fee record matched to an order and user, even those whose net rate is missing (feerate or rebrate NULL); only the average skips those records.
The net rate is NULL if either feerate or rebrate is NULL, so such records are left out of the average rather than treating a missing rebate as 0.
Inner joins drop fee records with no matching order or user. The 'plain average of per-scope averages' is the unweighted mean across scopes that have a non-NULL average.

alternatives.interpretation: Count only fee records that have a computable net rate (both feerate and rebrate non-NULL), so the count matches the records used in the average.
alternatives.sql: WITH j AS (SELECT u.acctscope AS acctscope, f.feerate - f.rebrate AS net_rate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault JOIN users u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp), s AS (SELECT acctscope, AVG(net_rate) AS avg_net_rate, COUNT(net_rate) AS fee_record_count FROM j GROUP BY acctscope) SELECT acctscope, avg_net_rate, fee_record_count, avg_net_rate - AVG(avg_net_rate) OVER () AS diff_from_avg_of_scope_avgs FROM s
